root_cause.text: macvlan_common_newlink() could publish a newly created macvlan net_device to RCU-protected lookup/forwarding paths before later failing, and its error path returned without waiting for an RCU grace period, allowing rtnl_newlink() to free the visible device while readers in macvlan_forward_source still accessed it.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly says “macvlan_common_newlink() might have made @dev visible before detecting an error, and its caller will directly call free_netdev(dev)” and the fix adds “synchronize_net()” with the comment “@dev might have been made visible before an error was detected... observe an RCU grace period before our caller (rtnl_newlink()) frees it”; the reported crash is a KASAN slab-use-after-free in macvlan_forward_source/macvlan_handle_frame.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: macvlan_common_newlink() could publish a newly created macvlan net_device to RCU-protected lookup/forwarding paths before later failing, and its error path returned without waiting for an RCU grace period, allowing rtnl_newlink() to free the visible device while readers in macvlan_forward_source still accessed it.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message explicitly says “macvlan_common_newlink() might have made @dev visible before detecting an error, and its caller will directly call free_netdev(dev)” and the fix adds “synchronize_net()” with the comment “@dev might have been made visible before an error was detected... observe an RCU grace period before our caller (rtnl_newlink()) frees it”; the reported crash is a KASAN slab-use-after-free in macvlan_forward_source/macvlan_handle_frame.

intent_record.intent_summary: Wait for an RCU grace period on macvlan link-creation failure to avoid freeing a device that may still be visible to concurrent readers.
intent_record.what: A new unconditional call to synchronize_net() was added on the error return path in macvlan_common_newlink(), immediately before returning err, along with a comment explaining that dev may have become visible before the error and that an RCU grace period must be observed before rtnl_newlink() frees it.
intent_record.how: This change makes the function wait for an RCU/network grace period before the caller can free the partially exposed net_device after a failure, preventing concurrent readers from accessing freed memory if the device became visible before the error was detected.

grouping_result.intent: Wait for an RCU grace period on macvlan link-creation failure to avoid freeing a device that may still be visible to concurrent readers.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds an RCU grace-period wait on macvlan link-creation failure so a newly published macvlan device is not freed while still reachable by RCU readers.

candidates.rationale: On the failure path after the new macvlan device may already have been published to RCU-protected readers, returning immediately lets higher layers free the device without first waiting for an RCU grace period, enabling use-after-free by concurrent readers.

vuln_statements.explanation: This immediate return on the macvlan_common_newlink() failure path omitted an RCU grace period even though the new macvlan device could already have been published to RCU-protected lookup/forwarding paths. As a result, callers could free the device while concurrent RCU readers still referenced it, causing the use-after-free.

index 4e238afab4a3..87e8d4cb4057 100644
--- a/drivers/n
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the full error-handling path around publication/registration in macvlan_common_newlink(). The vulnerable construct is still present: after `err = register_netdevice(dev);`, the function may fail and go to `destroy_port`, but the cleanup added here is only `if (list_empty(&port->vlans)) macvlan_port_destroy(lowerdev);` followed by `return err;`. There is no RCU grace-period wait such as `synchronize_rcu()` before returning on failure. Given the root cause, the issue is that the device/port can become visible to RCU-protected lookup/forwarding paths before later failure, and returning without an RCU wait allows later freeing while readers still access it. This commit only fixes port cleanup / memory leak handling (`goto destroy_port` and `macvlan_port_destroy(lowerdev)`), not the RCU-safety issue. Therefore the vulnerable construct remains present and the fix is not yet included.

In `macvlan_common_newlink()`, the device is linked into lookup/forwarding-visible structures before later operations that can fail: `list_add_tail_rcu(&vlan->list, &port->vlans);` and `hlist_add_head_rcu(&vlan->hlist, &port->vlan_hash[addr]);` occur before `err = register_netdevice(dev); if (err < 0) goto destroy_port;`. That means the device becomes visible to RCU-protected readers before `register_netdevice()` succeeds. The root cause says later failure can return without an RCU grace period, allowing free while readers still access it; this commit shows no added protection such as delaying publication until after successful registration, nor any RCU grace-period wait on the error path. diff --git a/drivers/net/macvlan.c b/drivers/net/macvlan.c
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..dc74d006e01f
--- /dev
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construction is visible in `macvlan_newlink()`. The function sets up `vlan->lowerdev`, `vlan->dev`, and `vlan->port`, then calls `err = register_netdevice(dev);` and immediately after exposes the new device via `list_add_tail(&vlan->list, &port->vlans);`. There is no protected rollback path after publication. More importantly, this version lacks any error handling after `register_netdevice(dev)` that would remove the device from RCU-visible lookup/forwarding structures and wait for an RCU grace period before returning an error. The root cause describes publication before later failure with missing `synchronize_rcu()` on the error path; this function has no such cleanup path at all. Related code shows RCU readers exist (`hlist_for_each_entry_rcu` in `macvlan_hash_lookup()` / `macvlan_broadcast()` and `rcu_dereference(skb->dev->macvlan_port)` in `macvlan_handle_frame()`), and teardown paths elsewhere explicitly use `synchronize_rcu()` (`macvlan_stop()` and `macvlan_port_destroy()`), confirming that RCU grace periods are required for safe removal. Since `macvlan_newlink()` contains no such post-publication failure cleanup, the bug is present and the fix is not.
